ShotGateSpec.description:
A permission-to-fire service the worker waits on before every shot.

The service streams ``safe`` / ``not_safe <reason>`` one way over TCP;
every SINGLESHOT waits for a ``safe`` received after the previous fire.
What that asks of the service: it sends a fresh ``safe`` once each
shot's cleanup is done (a shot with no state change would otherwise
hold the next until ``hold_pause_s``), and it accepts more than one
client (the worker and the web scanner's chip each hold a connection).
A service that repeats its state continuously needs ``holdoff_s``: the
time it takes to report a shot, so a ``safe`` from before it is ignored.

host.description: The service's host name or IP address on the facility network.
host.title: Host

hold_pause_s.description: Seconds a shot waits for permission before the scan pauses with the service's reason (resuming waits again; a pause never fires).
hold_pause_s.title: Hold Pause S

holdoff_s.description: Seconds after a shot before a 'safe' counts as the next shot's permission (0: any 'safe' received after the shot). Set it for a service that repeats its state continuously: the time the service takes to report a shot, so a 'safe' from before the shot is ignored.
holdoff_s.title: Holdoff S

TriggerState.description:
The named states the machine trigger can be driven to.

These names survived from the legacy system because they match how
operators think about the machine.

Attributes
----------
OFF : str
    Trigger fully stopped (used e.g. before timing synchronization).
STANDBY : str
    Between-steps idle: trigger free-runs but data-taking output (e.g.
    the gas jet) is off.
SCAN : str
    Taking data: trigger running with data-taking output on.
SINGLESHOT : str
    Fire exactly one shot (strict acquisition).
ARMED : str
    Ready for single shots: data-taking output on, trigger switched to
    single-shot source, waiting for SINGLESHOT commands.
TriggerState.title: TriggerState

TriggerWrite.description:
One device variable set during a state transition.

A transition is an ordered list of these; they are sent top to bottom.

device.description: The device to write to, e.g. 'U_DG645_ShotControl' or a gas-jet controller — any settable device can take part in a transition.
device.title: Device

variable.description: Which variable on the device to set, e.g. 'Trigger.Source'.
variable.title: Variable

value.description: The value to send, exactly as the device expects it — a number as text ('4.0'), a word ('on'), or a device option name ('External rising edges').
value.title: Value

TriggerWrite.title: TriggerWrite

description:
The device writes that drive the machine through its trigger states.

For each state (OFF, STANDBY, SCAN, SINGLESHOT, ARMED) list the writes —
possibly to several devices — that put the machine into it, **in the
order they should be sent**.  Edit it when timing hardware or its
settings change; make a separate profile for a different operating
condition (e.g. laser off).

Notes
-----
Values are sent verbatim over the GEECS wire protocol.  Use
:meth:`writes_for` / :meth:`defines_state` instead of digging the lists —
they implement the "state with no writes is not defined" rule.
:attr:`devices` lists every device the profile touches.

Format v2 removed the v1 ``variants`` overlay (see the module
docstring); a before-validator drops an empty v1 block, refuses a
populated one, and normalizes ``schema_version`` ≤ 1 to 2.

schema_version.description: Format version of this config file. Leave at 2 — tools update this automatically when the file format changes.
schema_version.title: Schema Version

name.description: The name scans use to refer to this trigger profile.
name.title: Name

states.description: For each trigger state, the writes that put the machine into it, applied in order from top to bottom. A transition may write several devices. Omit a device variable from a state to leave it untouched.
states.title: States

description.description: Optional note about what setup this profile is for.
description.title: Description

use_scan_mode.description: Run scans under this profile in GEECS scan mode, as Master Control drives the devices: the worker announces the scan to the experiment's devices (ScanStart), pushes each shot's save path to them before the fire, and ends the scan (ScanEnd) when the run closes. A device then acquires once per announced shot, saves shot-numbered files and applies its own database start/end values. Off by default. Strict acquisition only: a fly run and the calibration plans refuse such a profile. A profile with this flag and no writes at all is the box-less case — the shot message is the only trigger.
use_scan_mode.title: Use Scan Mode

shot_gate.description: A permission-to-fire service the worker waits on before every shot: a 'safe' received after the previous shot permits the next; unreachable or not safe holds it, and a long hold pauses the scan. Leave empty for no gate.

title: TriggerProfile
